epz_sez_zones.name: Silicon Valley (San Jose-SF)
epz_sez_zones.primary_focus: Global tech software & venture capital epicenter

tourism_enclaves.name: Orlando (Disney/Universal)
tourism_enclaves.spatial_impact: Geographically isolated mega-theme park spatial structures

core_periphery_zones.core: Northeast Corridor (Boston to Washington) & California Coastal Megacity Strip
core_periphery_zones.periphery: Central Appalachia, West Virginia coalfields & rural Montana Plains

topographic_friction_points.geopolitical_constraint: Rugged montane barrier historically slowing transcontinental integration but acting as a resource storehouse.
Historically restricted early European settlements to the Atlantic seaboard before westward expansion.

hydrological_arteries.strategic_advantage: World's largest contiguous system of navigable rivers, enabling low-cost freight transport and agricultural dominance.
Connects the industrial Great Lakes region directly with Atlantic maritime shipping lanes.

choke_points_vulnerabilities.impact: Crucial maritime bottleneck for commercial vessels sailing from Gulf Coast ports to the Atlantic.

buffer_zones.significance: Vast oceanic margins providing unparalleled strategic isolation and defense-in-depth against foreign states.

largest_diasporas.cultural_reach_impact: Strong influence on media consumption, shared consumer trends, significant cross-border cultural exchange.
Significant presence of retirees and expats, leading to fusion in border regions, real estate, and service industries.
Deep historical ties, shared language, strong influence on entertainment, business practices, and academic institutions.
Post-WWII military presence established long-standing communities, influencing local appreciation for American music, food, and traditions.
Historical colonial ties result in enduring American linguistic influence, media consumption, educational models, and pop culture.

examples: Fast food chains (McDonald's, KFC, Pizza Hut)

enclaves: American cultural centers (e.g., Benjamin Franklin House in London)
spatial_landscape.architectural_footprint: Skyscrapers, suburban sprawl, shopping malls, fast-food drive-thrus, industrial parks.
spatial_landscape.description: The American spatial landscape globally is characterized by the widespread presence of its commercial brands, entertainment venues, and architectural styles reflecting consumerism, efficiency, and a car-centric infrastructure, often adapted to local contexts but retaining recognizable features.

hybridity_and_glocalization.description: American fast-food chains adapting their menus and marketing strategies to cater to local tastes, dietary restrictions, and cultural preferences while maintaining their core brand identity.
Local film industries adopting narrative structures, genres, and production values popularized by Hollywood, often blending them with indigenous storytelling to create globally appealing content.
glocalized_examples: Bollywood action films with Hollywood-esque special effects
Korean blockbusters using Western narrative arcs
hybridity_and_glocalization.spatial_location: International film industries, local cinemas, streaming platforms.

hybridity_and_glocalization.description: Sports originating in the U.S. like basketball or baseball gaining popularity internationally, leading to the formation of local leagues and fan cultures that blend American rules and spectacle with local traditions.
glocalized_examples: Japanese Baseball (NPB) with unique fan chants and traditions
European basketball leagues adopting NBA marketing strategies
Streetball culture integrating local music and art globally
hybridity_and_glocalization.spatial_location: Sports stadiums, local sports clubs, media broadcasts worldwide.
